row_type: A (the archive's own dataset), its exact name composed as a generic enterprise category
classes_note: O-class not run on this pass: the field B supplies classes for other things sharing words with the name (enterprise AI registries, AI Overview trackers and scrapers), not for the registry, and none of its sources names the registry; the archive's own classes for the registry (a longitudinal research instrument, a founding dataset for machine-mediated reception studies, the Wound Gauge) are reached by the aliases. The aliases are the registry's proper name, its short name, its identifier, the field it founds and its gallery; 'capture registry' and 'machine-mediated reception' are broad and return many deposits that name the registry only as the place a capture is seated. Admission by reading (§3.4): a candidate is admitted when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim bearing on the registry (what it is, what a capture is, its method and protocol, its scoring and the PER and its dimensions, its priority and name, its versions, editions and surfaces, its reception as the archive records it); a header line, a related-identifier list, a link list, a citation of a capture slug or a bare mention of the registry as where a capture is kept is not a claim. A capture's transcript quoted in a deposit is reception, not an archive claim. The field's categories (enterprise AI registries such as Atlan, Collibra, trail, Alation; AI Overview trackers and scrapers such as Honeyb AI, Scrape.do, Octoparse, Advanced Web Ranking) are outside the alias set: none of their sources uses the name.
